title: Isomer distinction under equal composition
statement: Isomers have exactly equal retained composition but inequivalent complete connectivity or orientation signatures after every identity-preserving finite relabelling.
generation_rule: Generate the literal product of the registered isomer pair, composition, structure, equivalence, distinction, identity, record and extension choices.
grammar_boundary: Every finite pair of admitted chemical carriers with exactly equal composition signatures but unequal complete connectivity or held-orientation signatures after every identity-preserving relabelling.

choices.name: single-carrier-description
choices.reason: Isomerism compares at least two chemical carriers.

choices.name: equal-exact-composition
choices.reason: Element labels and positive multiplicities agree exactly.

choices.name: formula-equated-identity
choices.reason: A formula does not exhaust bonded organization.

choices.name: complete-structure-signatures
choices.reason: Connectivity and held orientation are compared.

choices.name: name-string-inequality
choices.reason: Different names can denote the same structure.

choices.name: all-identity-preserving-relabelings
choices.reason: Structural equality is tested under every finite allowed relabelling.

choices.name: equivalent-signatures
choices.reason: Equivalent complete signatures denote the same isomeric form.

choices.name: connectivity-or-orientation-difference
choices.reason: At least one retained structural relation differs.

choices.name: distinction-erased
choices.reason: Erasing the difference destroys the chemical question.

choices.name: separate-chemical-identities
choices.reason: Each surviving structure retains its own identity.

choices.name: isomer-label-only
choices.reason: A label cannot reproduce equality and difference.

choices.name: composition-and-structure-trace
choices.reason: Both composition and full comparison remain auditable.

choices.name: free-isomer-class
choices.reason: A free class label can manufacture a distinction.

choices.name: no-extra-rule
choices.reason: Equal composition plus structural inequivalence is sufficient.

induction_base: The first isomeric pair is the least generated equal-composition pair whose complete structural signatures are not related by an identity-preserving relabelling.
induction_step: Appending matched composition to both carriers preserves equality, while any retained unmatched connectivity or orientation relation preserves their distinction.
exclusions: no chemical dictionary, coordinate archive, fitted force field, measured geometry or V2 answer may select a candidate
no numerical zero, negative, irrational, imaginary or floating proof quantity
no free, fitted, learned or target-derived parameter
no application or opaque prediction result
no claim that topology alone predicts every measured coordinate or energy
external content remains inaccessible until after the consequence is sealed
Every finite pair of admitted chemical carriers with exactly equal composition signatures but unequal complete connectivity or held-orientation signatures after every identity-preserving relabelling.
operational_witnesses: chain and branched witnesses have equal exact composition
complete finite relabelling rejects chain/branch identity
a relabelled copy is structurally equivalent
falsification_condition: The claim fails if the official isomer record does not require equal composition with distinct structure or spatial arrangement, or if a changed row is accepted.
